domain: developer infrastructure / managed database tooling (Fly.io Managed Postgres)
proposition: Fly.io will ship flyctl (its official CLI) support for restoring an MPGv1 Postgres backup as an MPGv2 cluster, a capability that was announced as UI-only on 2026-08-11.
decision_relevance: Directly gates BCA candidate BC-0101 (candidate_type=NEW_MARKET, pain_severity=SEVERE, state=WATCH as of registration): the underlying pain (CLI-dependent migration workflows are blocked because this restore path exists only in the Fly.io web UI, not in flyctl) evaporates if Fly.io ships CLI support quickly, which would argue against BC-0101 remaining a live opportunity; if Fly.io does not add CLI support within the resolution window, that is stronger evidence the CLI/UI parity gap is a real, persistent constraint worth continued investigation.

resolution_question: By 2026-10-15, will Fly.io have shipped flyctl CLI support for restoring an MPGv1 Postgres backup as an MPGv2 cluster?
resolution_sources_expected: Fly.io official changelog (fly.io/docs/changelog or the Fly.io blog)
an official Fly.io staff reply in the cited community forum thread (https://community.fly.io/t/you-can-now-restore-your-mpgv1-backups-as-a-v2-cluster/28466)
positive_condition: Fly.io's official changelog, the flyctl GitHub release notes, or an official staff reply in the cited community forum thread confirms that flyctl supports restoring an MPGv1 Postgres backup as an MPGv2 cluster, on or before 2026-10-15.
negative_condition: An official Fly.io source (changelog, flyctl release notes, or a staff reply in the cited thread) explicitly states that flyctl CLI support for this restore path will not be added, or is deprioritized/indefinitely deferred, on or before 2026-10-15.
ambiguous_condition: The window closes on 2026-10-15 with no official statement either confirming or denying flyctl CLI support for this specific restore path (the restore may still be UI-only with no explicit decision publicly stated either way).
